attribution.note: Marcus states the prediction in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm prediction that companies will seek and find loopholes. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Documented company efforts identifying an exploitable gap fairly operationalize the prediction. Actual exploitation is appropriately unnecessary.

evidence.note: The rescission establishes the end of the order's operation, but establishes neither company discovery of loopholes nor its absence.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents no company episode satisfying the early-resolution rule and no comprehensive evidence against such conduct. Rescission does not settle the prediction, and no deadline was supplied.

attribution.note: Marcus gives his own assessment of the executive order.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the factual description and the probabilistic judgment about enforcement adequacy.

contract.note: The readings of breadth and some enforcement power are ordinary, but the contract grades only those components. It cannot assign a supported outcome to the full proposition while excluding its probabilistic adequacy judgment.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous order supports the factual description of broad coverage and mandatory provisions. It does not establish enforcement adequacy.
This official fact sheet supports the presence of compulsory reporting directions. It is an administration explanation, not an independent finding of effectiveness or adequacy.

reviews.rationale: The factual components receive support, but the full claim includes a probabilistic assessment of insufficient enforcement power without an adequacy standard. Policy excludes that assessment from scoring; the contract's narrower test cannot settle the whole normalized claim.
